title: Controlled Retrieval Fix Implementation -- Elliptical-Query Fallback + BM25 Startup Lifecycle
scope: Implemented ONLY the two fixes explicitly authorized: Phase 5C-1 (safe first-message fallback) and Phase 5C-2 (BM25 lifecycle wiring). No embedding, threshold, RRF, top_k, or reranker change. No subject-specific logic. No canonical data modified. No commit, no push.

baseline_before_changes.git_status: M team4a/docker-compose.yml (pre-existing, unrelated); rest untracked docs/reports from earlier phases

exact_files_changed.change: Removed the 'previous_user_turn is None' early-return branch inside RAGService.handle_query()'s is_elliptical_query() block. build_enriched_retrieval_query() is now called unconditionally when is_elliptical_query(query) is True -- it already returns the query unchanged when previous_user_turn is None, so retrieval now always runs on some query (enriched if a previous turn exists, unchanged otherwise) instead of being skipped entirely.
exact_files_changed.lines_changed: 48 lines changed (mostly a large explanatory comment replacing the old one)

exact_files_changed.change: Replaced test_missing_context_fresh_conversation_skips_retrieval_and_asks_for_clarification (asserted the OLD behavior: zero retrieval calls) with test_missing_context_fresh_conversation_still_attempts_plain_retrieval (asserts retrieval IS now attempted with the original, unenriched query). test_missing_context_turn_is_still_persisted required no change and still passes.

Replaced test_elliptical_followup_produces_citations_from_actual_retrieval_only (asserted zero citations for a fresh-conversation elliptical query) with test_elliptical_query_with_no_history_still_retrieves_on_the_original_query (asserts real citations from real retrieval).

Added a FastAPI `lifespan` async context manager that calls the existing, cached get_hybrid_retriever().refresh_bm25_corpus() exactly once at process startup, before the app accepts requests. Wrapped in try/except so a failure logs an error and the app still starts (non-fatal, matching the optional-reranker precedent already established elsewhere in this codebase). Also added logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) -- required because no logging configuration existed anywhere in the app, which was silently suppressing ALL INFO-level logs including this new startup log line and the pre-existing 'BM25 corpus refreshed' line inside refresh_bm25_corpus() itself.

Docstring-only update: the module's own 'SCOPE NOTE' previously stated BM25 population was entirely out of scope for the live application. Updated to reflect that app/api/main.py's lifespan now closes that gap, using this module's own existing get_hybrid_retriever() -- no new BM25 wiring added in this file itself.

behavior_changed.before: IF is_elliptical_query(query) is True AND there is no previous user turn in the conversation THEN: HybridRetriever.retrieve() is never called; retrieval_results is hard-set to []; LLMGenerator.generate_conversational() (the same ungrounded path used for casual greetings) produces a scripted clarifying-question reply.
behavior_changed.after: IF is_elliptical_query(query) is True AND there is no previous user turn THEN: build_enriched_retrieval_query(query, None) returns the query unchanged, and HybridRetriever.retrieve() is called normally with the ORIGINAL query. If retrieval finds relevant evidence, LLMGenerator.generate() produces a normal grounded, cited answer. If retrieval genuinely finds nothing relevant, LLMGenerator.generate()'s own pre-existing, already-tested behavior returns INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_MESSAGE (no LLM call, no fabrication risk) -- an honest non-answer instead of a scripted clarification.
behavior_changed.unaffected: Genuine follow-ups (a real previous user turn exists) are completely unchanged: build_enriched_retrieval_query() still enriches the retrieval query with the previous turn's text exactly as before. Casual greetings ('Hi', 'Thanks', etc.) are unaffected -- they are gated by the separate is_casual_message() check, evaluated earlier in handle_query() and not touched by this change.

phase5c1_test_results.focused_suite: team4b/tests/test_followup_context.py + team4b/tests/test_rag_service.py: 71 passed (same count as baseline; one test rewritten to assert the new, correct behavior)
phase5c1_test_results.test_api_suite: 127 passed (one test rewritten analogously to assert the new, correct behavior at the HTTP route level)
phase5c1_test_results.genuine_followup_regression: test_elliptical_followup_enriches_retrieval_with_previous_user_turn, test_topic_switch_then_elliptical_followup_uses_the_new_topic, and all other genuine-follow-up tests pass unchanged -- enrichment behavior with a real previous turn is untouched.

targeted_19_case_retest.method: Re-ran all 19 previously-failing queries (10 from round-2 clean corpus, 9 from round-1 mismatched corpus) against the isolated validation environment with the Phase 5C-1 fix live.
targeted_19_case_retest.result_summary: 19/19 (100%) now return non-zero citations and a grounded answer, up from 0/19 before the fix.

targeted_19_case_retest.quality_spot_check: Manually reviewed full answer text (not just citation presence) for DS-10, DB-01, MA-08, EN-01, NS-01, SEC-DOC-01: all are genuinely correct, well-grounded, properly-cited answers, matching exactly the content independently identified as present in Phase 5B's diagnostic trace (e.g. DB-01's 5 citation pages [1,6,1,5,12] match Phase 5B's counterfactual trace exactly). OS-01 is the one notable case: it still returns citations (5, from the workspace's own weak/ML-adjacent video content, a corpus-composition issue flagged separately in Phase 5B) but the model HONESTLY DECLINES rather than fabricating an OS answer from irrelevant content -- exactly the desired 'insufficient-evidence, not a fabricated topic' outcome.

workspace_document_isolation_verificatio.method: Re-ran WI-01..04 (each asks one workspace about content exclusive to a different workspace) against the fixed environment.
workspace_document_isolation_verificatio.result: 0/4 showed any cross-workspace citation -- isolation fully intact after the fix.

bm25_startup_verification.notes: Required an additional, minimal logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) fix in app/api/main.py -- confirmed via code search that NO logging configuration existed anywhere in the app, so this INFO-level log line (and the pre-existing one inside refresh_bm25_corpus() itself) was being silently dropped by Python's default logging behavior even before this phase's changes. This is a visibility fix only; it does not change what is logged, only whether it is shown.

control_query_score_distribution.query: What are the layers of the OSI model? (Computer Networks workspace)
control_query_score_distribution.interpretation: Scores are no longer capped near 0.5 -- direct, empirical confirmation that BM25 is now genuinely contributing a second ranked list to Reciprocal Rank Fusion, exactly as the RRF formula was always designed to combine.

semantic_bm25_rrf_evidence.workspace_document_filtering_in_both_leg: Re-confirmed intact by direct code reading of _retrieve_hybrid() (unchanged by this phase's edits) -- collection_filter, workspace_id, and document_ids are still threaded into both the vector_future and bm25_future before fusion.

btree_before_after.query: What is a B-tree and how does node splitting work during insertion?
btree_before_after.improvement: BM25 alone ranks the target chunk #1 of 746 (exact-term match on 'B-tree'/'node'/'splitting'/'insertion'). Fusing it with the semantic leg via RRF improves the chunk's overall rank from 29th to 9th -- a ~3x improvement -- and its normalized score from 0.343 to 0.843, both far above the unchanged 0.3 threshold. It still does not crack the top-5 cutoff: 8 other chunks from the same 129-chunk, heavily tree/BST-themed PDF also score well on both legs (general tree/BST content that shares significant vocabulary with the B-tree passage).
btree_before_after.live_end_to_end_confirmation: Re-ran the exact query against the real, fixed, BM25-populated validation environment via the real chat API: the final answer's 5 citations are pages [119, 98, 127, 99, 120] -- page 128 is confirmed absent. The model correctly stated it could not find specific information on B-tree node splitting, rather than fabricating an answer -- consistent, honest behavior even though the best evidence didn't make the final cut.
btree_before_after.note: Per explicit instruction, top_k was NOT changed even though it would be the direct lever to rescue this specific case. This is documented as a remaining, known limitation for a future phase, not addressed here.

latency_impact.startup: +1.23 seconds one-time cost per process start (measured), to scroll and index 4938 chunks (validation collection; would scale with canonical/production collection size -- 542 points, so proportionally faster there).
latency_impact.per_query: No structural change to per-query latency -- BM25 search itself is fast (in-memory BM25Okapi over a workspace-scoped subset; historically measured at ~0.137s per query in the Phase 4C report for a 1650-chunk corpus) and runs in parallel with the semantic leg via the existing ThreadPoolExecutor, unchanged. Query-to-query latency in this phase's own tests remained dominated by CPU-only Ollama generation (11.5s-179.8s across the 19 retested queries), consistent with every prior validation round -- not attributable to this phase's changes.

regression_results.note: This test was NOT modified. It remains the same, pre-existing, already-documented stale ground-truth chunk-ID mismatch from the post-Docker-incident rebuild (see docs/m6-historical-vs-rebuilt-rag-comparison.md), unrelated to this phase's changes.

remaining_known_limitations: DS-11 (B-tree case): BM25 populated the correct chunk to rank 1 and improved the fused rank from 29th to 9th, but it still does not crack the top-5 cutoff. top_k was deliberately left unchanged per this phase's explicit scope. A future phase would need to evaluate whether increasing top_k, enabling the reranker (Phase 4B's already-built, currently-disabled component), or another ranking-quality change is justified -- not decided here.

OS-01/OS-04 (Operating Systems workspace): retrieval now runs (Phase 5C-1 fixed), but this workspace's own candidate pool is independently weak (video content that is partly ML-adjacent, per Phase 5B's corpus-composition finding) -- the model now correctly gives an honest 'insufficient evidence' answer instead of a scripted clarification, which is the correct, desired outcome, but it is not a 'good answer' either. This is a corpus-composition characteristic of this specific validation workspace, not something this phase's code changes could or should address.

F3 (hallucinated prior-conversation context, ML-07/OOS-01 from the prior validation report) was NOT investigated or fixed in this phase -- explicitly out of scope per the task's own instruction not to implement conversation-faithfulness hardening unless this phase's own changes directly exposed a related regression. No such regression was found.

F4 (casual-intent classifier's narrow phrase list, e.g. 'Great'/'Okay'/'What can you do?' not recognized as casual) was NOT investigated or fixed in this phase -- a separate, deliberately-scoped classifier (casual_intent.py) untouched by either of this phase's two fixes.
Cross-language retrieval (F2, Hindi query -> English source misses) was NOT investigated or fixed in this phase -- unrelated to either of the two mechanisms fixed here.

BM25 corpus freshness after this phase's fix is still a one-time, startup-only refresh -- newly-ingested content after the process starts will not be reflected in BM25 search until a future restart or an explicit future re-refresh mechanism, exactly as already documented in refresh_bm25_corpus()'s own long-standing docstring. Not changed or newly introduced by this phase.

another_retrieval_change_justified.verdict: NOT DECIDED IN THIS PHASE -- correctly out of scope.
another_retrieval_change_justified.reasoning: The B-tree case's before/after ranking (29 -> 9) demonstrates BM25 population provides a real, substantial ranking-quality improvement, but is not sufficient on its own to guarantee every precision-relevant chunk reaches the final top-5 in a densely-related-content workspace. Whether top_k, the reranker, or another mechanism should be the next lever is a decision for a future, explicitly-scoped phase (per this phase's own instruction not to change top_k or enable the reranker here) -- this report documents the evidence for that decision, it does not make it.
